biography:
Michelle David is an American soul and gospel singer born on August 28, 1966, in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. Raised in New York from age ten, she began her musical journey in church at just four years old and joined her first gospel group, The Mission of Love, at age five. Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, David built an impressive career performing in Broadway productions including Mama, I Want To Sing, The Sound of Motown, Glory of Gospel, and Mahalia, while also contributing background vocals for legendary artists Diana Ross and Michael Bolton. Her early training at the Fame School of Performing Arts and her deep roots in gospel music shaped her distinctive vocal style and artistic sensibility.

Since relocating to the Netherlands in 1994, David has established herself as a contemporary soul powerhouse. In 2015, she formed Michelle David & The True-tones with guitarist Paul Willemsen, bassist Onno Smit, and drummer Bas Bouma, releasing seven critically acclaimed albums that blend traditional gospel with modern soul, funk, rock, and afro-beat influences. The group's innovative approach to gospel—infusing classic ecclesiastic pieces with contemporary arrangements and diverse musical inspirations—has earned them an Edison nomination and established them as a must-see live act. They have performed at major European festivals including Pinkpop and North Sea Jazz, toured extensively across Europe and beyond, and even performed at the 2022 Winter Olympics.

David's artistry is defined by her powerful vocals, emotional depth, and willingness to push gospel music into fresh sonic territories. With The True-tones, she has created a distinctive sound characterized by groovy basslines, upbeat grooves, and strong melodies that resonate with audiences worldwide. Her work represents a pioneering approach to contemporary gospel, honoring tradition while embracing modern influences and creating an authentic musical experience that transcends generational boundaries.
name: Michelle David
